_doc: Every tunable for the QQQ drift-harvest arm. Values here override the dataclass defaults in config.py. Section numbers refer to ALGORITHM.md. Editing this file changes strategy behavior on the next cycle — it is operator territory, and every change should be recorded in the commit message.

instrument._doc: 1 unit = 100 shares = 1 option contract's worth of underlying (ALGORITHM.md §2).

cadence._doc: Daily cycle at 06:35 PT = 09:35 ET, five minutes after the open (moved from 12:45 PT on 2026-09-03 at operator request). Not 09:30 exactly: the opening auction is the widest-spread period of the session and this engine SELLS the short leg, so it pays that spread directly on every entry. Intraday passes run at :00/:15/:30/:45, 27 per normal session, and are defensive only — they never open positions (§10). NOTE: the backtest decides on daily CLOSE bars, so live decisions now use different prices than the tested ones; that divergence is unmeasured.

ladder._doc: §5. Multiplier 0.0 is the reference level itself — tracked for anti-clustering but never a buy zone. Recenter threshold of 0.5 ATR is the agreed starting value; the source doc left 'meaningful new high' open.
ladder._trade_at_reference_note: TRUE, and now backtested rather than assumed. DEVIATES FROM ALGORITHM.md 5, which excludes the reference level from tradeable zones ('at the highs', Phase A). Over 626 sessions (2024-03-01..2026-08-28): false -> $128,369, 28.37%, 11.34% DD, Sharpe 0.98; true -> $130,721, 30.72%, 11.17% DD, Sharpe 1.06, with spreads written rising 41 -> 76. Better return, lower drawdown and higher Sharpe together. Note what this implies: at false the strategy's Sharpe (0.98) is BELOW buy-and-hold's (0.99), so the doc's design as translated has no edge over simply owning QQQ on this sample — the deviation is what creates one. Single sample; the conclusion is regime-dependent and should be re-tested when more option history is available.
ladder._zone_rearm_note: Days before a used acquisition zone becomes available again. KEEP AT 0. 0 is ALGORITHM.md 5's rule: a zone is spent until the ladder recenters on a new high. Re-arming was proposed because the engine wrote zero spreads through the Feb-Apr 2025 decline, which looked like a defect. Backtested 2024-03-01..2026-08-28 (626 sessions) it is not: 0 days -> 28.15% return, 12.04% max DD, Sharpe 0.90; 5 days -> 27.20%, 25.38% DD, Sharpe 0.61; 10 days -> 27.64%, 22.02% DD, 0.65; 21 days -> 28.11%, 16.77% DD, 0.80. Re-arming does make the engine trade the decline (0 -> 54/42/22 spreads in the fall, as intended) and every variant returns LESS while roughly doubling drawdown. Selling puts into a falling market writes contracts that then go in-the-money. The anti-clustering rule is protecting the strategy, not hobbling it. Left configurable so the idea is not re-proposed from intuition, with the evidence against it recorded here.
ladder._accumulate_note: 50, ENABLED 2026-09-03 for a $250,000 account. It was 0 while the account was $100,000, and correctly so: at that size it converted alpha into beta — absolute return rose only because the position was larger, the edge over buy-and-hold of the SAME share count halved from $8,471 to $4,980, Sharpe fell 1.04 -> 1.01 and drawdown rose 12.40% -> 16.12%. At $250,000 it inverts. Over the same 626 sessions: accumulation OFF gives $12,648/yr, 4.81% DD, Sharpe 1.03 on 100 shares; ON gives $28,746/yr, 9.84% DD, Sharpe 1.08 on 254 shares — against buy-and-hold of 250 shares at $27,080/yr, 11.26% DD, Sharpe 0.99. Higher return, LOWER drawdown and higher Sharpe than equivalent beta. The capital is finally sufficient to carry the exposure §15 asks for. REVERT TO 0 if the account ever drops back toward $100,000.

regime._doc: §4. BULL = price > 200DMA and slope > band; DEFENSIVE = price < 200DMA and slope < -band; else NEUTRAL. flat_band 0.0 means no dead zone, matching the doc.
regime._filter_note: ENABLED 2026-09-03, on judgement rather than measurement — and the distinction matters. V5 §4/§20/§24 specify that the regime should change accumulation aggressiveness, ATR spacing, put selection and call aggressiveness; until now it was computed, logged and displayed while NOTHING branched on it. Now wired. BULL multipliers are all 1.0 by design, so the filter can only ever WITHDRAW risk relative to the tested behaviour, never add it. MEASURED EFFECT IS ~NIL: over 626 sessions, off -> $12,648/yr, Sharpe 1.03; on -> $12,510/yr, Sharpe 1.01 (accumulation off). With accumulation on, drawdown improves slightly, 9.84% -> 9.73%. The reason is that the window was 66% BULL, 26.5% NEUTRAL and only 7.5% DEFENSIVE — the filter is a no-op in two thirds of the sample and barely acts in the rest. It is enabled because it is insurance against the regime the data does not contain, not because the backtest endorses it. Published support is indirect but strong: a 2005-2025 SPX study of 45-DTE 16-delta short premium reports Sharpe 0.52 unfiltered versus 0.81 filtered. Expect no visible benefit until the first real downtrend.

exposure_curve._doc: ALGORITHM.md 6. Target unit-equivalent exposure keyed to decline from reference. OPERATOR CHANGE 2026-09-03: base lifted from 1.0 to 1.25 at the highs (whole curve +0.25) so the engine has genuine appetite above the core rather than sitting exactly at target and proposing nothing. The doc's original was 1.0/1.5/2.0/2.5/3.0/3.125/3.25. Still an untested hypothesis either way - the source doc labels this table as one.

put_engine._doc: §7. short_delta_target 0.20 is the midpoint of the 15-25 test range. max_risk_reward_ratio null disables the quality filter. profit_capture_pct is NOT yet enforced — needs a live per-position mark (§11).
put_engine._profit_capture_note: NOW WIRED (2026-09-03); it was specified in ALGORITHM.md 7 but never implemented, so the only exit was the 3-DTE force close and every spread was held through the highest-gamma stretch of its life. Backtested 2024-03-01..2026-08-28: off -> 28.15% return, 12.04% max DD, Sharpe 0.90, overlay $1,283, 14.2% of credit kept. On -> 40%: 31.09%/11.11%/1.07/$4,235/43.0%; 50%: 30.92%/11.18%/1.05/$4,060; 60%: 30.75%/11.26%/1.03/$3,889; 80%: 30.65%/11.62%/1.00. Better return, lower drawdown and higher Sharpe together. Set to 50 rather than the best-measured 40 because the 40-60 spread is inside one sample's noise and picking the edge of a tested range is how you overfit; 50 is also the standard convention among premium sellers.
put_engine._risk_reward_note: 10.0 — ALGORITHM.md 7's documented default. Briefly set to 5.0 on 2026-09-03 because a sweep over 2024-03..2026-08 put it marginally ahead ($129,039 vs $128,658, i.e. 0.3%, inside noise). Reverted the same day: on the live 2026-09 chain NO protective leg achieves 5:1 — the best available is 6.8:1 — so the filter refused every spread and the arm could not trade at all. The sweep optimised a metric without checking the winner was reachable in the current regime, which is a good way to tune a strategy into inactivity. 8:1, 10:1 and unrestricted produced BYTE-IDENTICAL backtest results because max-loss-aware leg selection already caps proposals below 8:1 in that window; 10 is chosen over 8 because it additionally admits today's 16-wide spread at 8.3:1, which carries the most premium of any leg that fits the loss cap.
put_engine._contracts_note: KEEP AT 1. Swept 1-4 contracts over 626 sessions and the result is non-monotonic: edge over buy-and-hold ran $3,642 / $1,338 / $8,471 / $4,353 for 1/2/3/4, and Sharpe 1.06 / 0.90 / 1.04 / 1.00. The swing between adjacent settings exceeds the total edge of most of them, so this is path dependence — which spreads happened to be open when the market moved — not a size effect. 3 looks best on this sample and choosing it would be overfitting. 1 has the highest Sharpe and the lowest drawdown. Revisit only with more than one market sample.
put_engine._leg_selection_note: 'widest' takes the most premium the max-loss cap allows; 'best_risk_reward' takes the best loss-to-profit ratio. They differ because risk/reward is U-shaped in width — the best ratio on the 2026-09 chain is at width 7 (6.82:1) while the widest that fits at 1% is width 16 (8.33:1). Backtested: widest wins at both caps ($130,737 / $130,919 vs $130,326 for best_risk_reward at either). Why: with a 50% profit-capture exit the position is closed long before either extreme of the ratio is reached, so the credit collected matters more than a max-loss-to-max-profit figure the strategy almost never realises. Risk/reward is close to the wrong metric for this strategy.
put_engine._dte_note: 21-35, unchanged — V5 §9. Tested against a shorter window on the hypothesis that it would collect more premium; it collects LESS. Over 626 sessions at $250k with accumulation off: 5-14 DTE -> $13,057/yr gross premium, $932 net, Sharpe 0.99; 7-14 -> $13,594 / $1,061 / 1.00; 14-21 -> $17,423 / $1,632 / 1.03; 21-35 -> $19,756 / $1,626 / 1.03; 30-45 -> $21,963 / $1,606 / 0.99. Gross premium rises monotonically with DTE. The reason is that the number of spreads written is nearly constant across every window (79-84): TRADE COUNT IS GATED BY THE LADDER ZONES, NOT BY EXPIRY. Shortening the window therefore just collects less per trade at the same frequency. 14-21 is marginally ahead of 21-35 and statistically tied with it; kept at the spec's value. To collect more premium the lever is more entries, not shorter expiries.

call_engine._doc: §8. min_effective_sale_vs_reference 1.0 means strike+premium must be >= reference price: never monetize excess inventory below the level that triggered accumulating it. Core unit is never capped.

dividend._doc: §8 QQQ-specific. Refuse a call straddling ex-div whose extrinsic value is below 1.25x the dividend — that is when early assignment becomes rational for the holder. MNQ has no equivalent.

risk._doc: §9 gates 1-3 are max_loss_per_spread / max_aggregate_put_risk / max_crash_stress. The doc allows crash-stress up to 0.20; 0.15 is the stricter default. daily_loss_limit_pct and max_drawdown_pct drive core/circuit_breaker.py and are NOT from the source doc — they are platform-level backstops. Both are set wide because equity here includes the mark-to-market of a core position the strategy is designed to hold through corrections; a tight daily limit would trip the breaker in exactly the drawdown the ladder wants to buy.
risk._equity_basis_note: REMOVED 2026-09-03, and the reason matters. It was introduced because the core breached the crash-stress cap and no spread could be written. That breach was an implementation error, not a real limit: V5 §31 caps the loss under a -20% shock, while the code capped the WORST of §30's -5/-10/-15/-20/-30% shocks. Under the actual rule the core loses 14.3% of real equity, inside the 15% cap, and no override is needed. Caps now size against true account equity.
risk._crash_stress_note: 0.15 — §31's lower bound, binding on the -20% shock as §31 specifies. Left at 15% deliberately: at $250,000 the cap is IRRELEVANT. A sweep of 10/15/18/20% produced byte-identical results because the gate never binds at this account size — 254 shares is $182,174 of exposure, losing 14.6% of equity under a -20% shock, and the actual constraints are the ladder zones and available cash. Raising it buys nothing and only removes a backstop that costs nothing to keep. At $100,000 the picture was different: 10% beat 15% on every measure but blocked all trading at QQQ 717, and 20% was identical to 15%.
risk._max_loss_per_spread_note: 0.01, back to V5 §10's hard limit. It was briefly 0.02, which is outside §36's own test range of 0.5/0.75/1/1.5% and gave up more per-trade risk than the spec contemplates.

backtest._doc: §11. Historical greeks are Black-Scholes approximations (IV backed out of the quoted mid) because Polygon's historical endpoints carry no greeks. The chain walk makes one quotes request per contract, so polygon_max_workers is pinned to 1 and requests are spaced by polygon_min_interval_seconds to stay under the ~100 req/min plan cap.

cash_sweep._doc: NOT from ALGORITHM.md — added 2026-09-03. The strategy carries ~$28,500 idle on a $100k account because the core consumes the capital and the options program risks only a few thousand at a time. Idle cash earned nothing in every backtest, which costs more than the options overlay produces: ~$1,283/yr at 4.5% versus ~$1,620/yr from every spread written. SGOV is 0-3 month Treasuries, near-zero duration risk. The reserve is the aggregate put-risk cap plus reserve_buffer, so the options program can always open, close or take assignment without a forced sale — holding slightly too much cash costs a few dollars of yield, holding too little forces a liquidation at the worst possible moment.
